On the 600 and 700 maps, this label covers southern Sumatra, western Java and southern Borneo, where small kingdoms had taken up Indian ideas of kingship, Sanskrit and Hindu and Buddhist religion.

The oldest inscriptions of the islands come from such states. In eastern Borneo, King Mulavarman of Kutai set up stone posts with Sanskrit verses around 400. In western Java, King Purnavarman of Tarumanagara carved his footprints and deeds in stone in the 5th century. In Sumatra, the Melayu kingdom around Jambi sent envoys to China.

These kingdoms lived on trade between India and China. In the late 600s one of them, Srivijaya at Palembang, swallowed its neighbours and took control of the straits. The Chinese monk Yijing stayed there in 671 to study Sanskrit; see Yijing at Srivijaya.
sum: On the 600 and 700 maps, this label covers southern Sumatra, western Java and southern Borneo, where small kingdoms had taken up Indian ideas of kingship, Sanskrit and Hindu and Buddhist religion.
